authentication.notes: Every route reads the Authorization header. The WebSocket upgrade additionally accepts the credential as a subprotocol offer, because a browser cannot set headers on an upgrade - see websocket.auth.

principals.viewer: Every *.read permission plus telemetry.stream; no mutation.

envelope.notes: Every success body is {data, correlation_id}; every failure body is {error:{code,message,correlation_id}}. The same id is echoed in the X-Correlation-ID response header, and a client may propose one with an X-Correlation-ID request header.

discovery_busy.message: A discovery run is already pending.

authentication_required.meaning: No Authorization header on an authenticated deployment.

conflicting_bearer_credentials.meaning: Upgrade carried both an Authorization header and a bearer subprotocol offer that do not present the same credential.

http_error.meaning: Generic transport failure; the HTTP status carries the meaning.

method_not_allowed.meaning: Endpoint exists but not for this method.

not_found.meaning: No such endpoint, or that capability is not composed.

origin_not_allowed.meaning: Origin header outside the configured CORS allowlist.

permission_denied.meaning: Authenticated principal lacks this route's permission.

rate_limited.meaning: Per subject:action command budget exhausted; see Retry-After.

unsupported_subprotocol.meaning: Upgrade offered a Sec-WebSocket-Protocol value this endpoint will not echo; refused before the handshake.

limits._note: Transport limits are the ControlPlaneHttpConfig defaults, which a deployment may override in config/control_plane.yml; treat them as the expected shape, not as constants. websocket_max_inbound_message_bytes bounds client-to-server frames only - server-to-client frames such as telemetry_snapshot are not capped by it.

auth._note: Send the credential through exactly one carrier. Both carriers on one upgrade must present the same credential in the same bearer form, otherwise the upgrade is refused with 401 conflicting_bearer_credentials. Any other Sec-WebSocket-Protocol offer is refused with 400 unsupported_subprotocol before the handshake, so it never reaches a log.

subprotocol.disabled_when: A configured credential uses a character outside credential_charset; the deployment then logs one startup warning and this carrier is unavailable, with no fallback.
subprotocol.precedence: The Authorization header wins when both are present.

error_codes.invalid_stream_message: Client frame was not a JSON object.
error_codes.rate_limited: Client frame budget exhausted; the socket then closes.
error_codes.unsupported_stream_message: Client frame type is neither ping nor resync.

error.retry_after_seconds: integer, present only on the rate_limited variant, which is immediately followed by a close
